title: What is LLP Company? Full Form, Benefits, Registration Process & Fees in India
summary: What is LLP company? Explore Limited Liability Partnership meaning in business, benefits, registration steps, costs & annual compliance in India.

Toggle


### TL;DR


LLP stands for **Limited Liability Partnership** . It combines partnership-style management with a separate legal identity and limited partner liability. An LLP needs at least two partners and two designated partners, has no prescribed minimum capital and is governed mainly by its LLP agreement. It often suits professional and closely held businesses, while a private limited company may be better for equity fundraising.


##


**What Is an LLP? Full Form and Meaning**


The full form of LLP is **Limited Liability Partnership** . Formed under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, it combines partnership flexibility with legal separation and limited liability.


People often search for “what is an LLP company” or “LLP full form in company.” Legally, however, an LLP is not a company registered under the Companies Act, 2013. It is a body corporate with its own legal identity. It can own property, enter contracts, open bank accounts, sue and be sued in its own name.


This distinction matters when comparing an LLP with a[private limited company](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/private-limited-company-explained/) or a[sole proprietorship](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-sole-proprietorship/) . The right structure depends on liability, compliance, taxation and funding plans.


### **Key Features of LLP Company**


- **Separate Legal Entity** : LLP owns property, signs contracts, and pursues legal action independently from partners
- **Limited Liability** : Partners’ personal assets protected; creditors claim only LLP assets
- **Perpetual Succession** : Partner changes do not dissolve the entity; the business continues indefinitely
- **Flexible Management** : LLP agreement determines profit sharing and operations without mandatory board meetings
- **No Minimum Capital** : Partners start with any agreed contribution amount


**Requirement** **Details**


**Minimum Partners** 2 partners, who may be individuals or eligible body corporates


**Designated Partners** At least 2 individuals


**Resident requirement** At least 1 designated partner must satisfy the current “resident in India” test under the LLP Act


**Maximum partners** No statutory upper limit


**Minimum capital** No prescribed minimum contribution


**Foreign participation** Permitted subject to applicable FEMA, FDI, KYC and sectoral rules


##


How Liability Works in an LLP


The liability of a partnership depends heavily on its legal structure. In a traditional partnership firm, partners may be personally and jointly liable for the firm’s obligations. In an LLP, the LLP’s obligations are generally its own, and a partner is not personally liable solely because of being a partner.


Limited liability is not absolute. A partner remains personally liable for their own wrongful act or omission. The protection may also be lost in cases involving fraud. If an existing partnership firm converts into an LLP, the partners can remain personally liable for obligations incurred before conversion. These principles are set out in the[Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/2023/1/A2009-06.pdf) .


An LLP protects one partner from automatic personal liability for another partner’s misconduct, but not from their own fraud, negligence or contractual guarantees.

##


Benefits of an LLP in India


### Separate Legal Identity and Business Continuity


An LLP can hold property, sign contracts and maintain banking relationships in its own name. Its existence continues when a partner joins, retires or dies.


### Flexible Internal Management


Partners can define profit sharing, voting rights, responsibilities and exit rules through the LLP agreement, without following a company’s board and share-capital framework.


### Limited Liability for Partners


Personal assets are generally separated from ordinary LLP debts, offering more protection than a traditional partnership.


### Comparatively Focused Compliance


LLPs generally have fewer corporate governance formalities than companies. However, annual MCA filings, books of account, income-tax returns and applicable GST, TDS or event-based filings still need attention.


##


How LLP Taxation Works in India


An Indian LLP is generally taxed as a firm. It should not be described as a U.S.-style pass-through entity in which all business profit is automatically taxed at each partner’s individual rate.


The LLP pays tax on its taxable income. A partner’s share of profit from an LLP that has been separately assessed is generally exempt in the partner’s hands under Section 10(2A). Interest, remuneration or other amounts paid to partners can receive different tax treatment and are subject to the LLP agreement and the Income-tax Act. The[Income Tax Department’s guidance on tax-free income](https://www.incometaxindia.gov.in/Tutorials/11.Tax%20free%20incomes%20final.pdf) explains this distinction.


Tax rates and Alternate Minimum Tax provisions can change, so confirm the current position instead of selecting a structure only on a headline rate.


##


LLP vs Partnership Firm vs Private Limited Company


Factor LLP Partnership firm Private limited company


Legal status Separate legal entity Firm and partners are not fully separate in the same way Separate legal entity


Owner liability Generally limited, subject to exceptions Generally unlimited personal liability Generally limited to unpaid share capital or guarantee


Internal governance Primarily LLP agreement Partnership deed and Partnership Act Companies Act, articles and board/shareholder processes


Continuity Perpetual succession Depends on the deed and applicable law Perpetual succession


Equity shares Cannot issue company shares Cannot issue company shares Can issue shares, subject to law


Typical fit Professional and closely held businesses Small, relationship-led businesses accepting personal liability Businesses planning equity funding, ESOPs or larger governance structures


Choose an LLP when limited liability and flexible partner-led management matter more than issuing equity shares. Choose a private limited company when the planned ownership, employee incentives or institutional fundraising model needs a share-based structure.

##


LLP Registration Process in India


LLP incorporation is completed online through the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The exact workflow can change with MCA form updates, but the main sequence is consistent.


### Step 1: Obtain Digital Signature Certificates


Apply for Class 3 DSC for all designated partners through authorized certificate agencies. DSC enables digital signing of all MCA forms and future filings.


### Step 2: Reserve the LLP Name


Use the applicable MCA name-reservation service and propose a distinctive name ending in “LLP.” Check existing company and LLP names as well as trademarks before filing.


### Step 3: File the Incorporation Form


Submit FiLLiP with the proposed business activity, registered office, partner and designated partner details, contribution information and supporting documents. Where permitted, identification numbers for proposed designated partners may be allotted through the incorporation process.


### Step 4: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation


After approving the incorporation filing, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and LLP Identification Number, or LLPIN. An LLP receives an LLPIN, not a[Corporate Identity Number or CIN](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/corporate-identification-number-cin/) .


### Step 5: Execute and File the LLP Agreement


The partners should execute the agreement with the applicable state stamp duty and file its details in Form 3 within the prescribed period, generally 30 days from incorporation. The agreement should clearly cover contribution, profit sharing, authority, decision-making, dispute resolution and partner exits.


### Step 6: Complete Tax and Operating Registrations


Complete PAN and TAN requirements, open a[business bank account](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/how-to-open-business-bank-account-in-india/) , and assess whether the LLP needs[GST registration](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-registration-online-process-documents/) ,[Udyam registration](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/udyam-registration-online/) or an[Import Export Code](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/what-is-import-export-code-iec/) . The LLP should also keep its[business PAN documentation](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/business-pan-card-how-to-apply-online-documents-required/) consistent across tax, banking and payment accounts.


##


Eligibility and Documents Required for LLP Registration


An LLP needs at least two partners and two designated partners. Only individuals can act as designated partners, although eligible body corporates may become partners and nominate individuals to act on their behalf. At least one designated partner must meet the current statutory residence requirement.


Common documents include:


- PAN and identity proof for Indian partners
- Recent address proof for each proposed partner
- Passport and appropriately notarised or apostilled documents for foreign nationals, where applicable
- Registered-office proof, such as an ownership document or rent agreement
- Owner’s no-objection certificate for rented premises
- A recent utility bill for the registered office
- Digital Signature Certificates for the persons signing the forms
- Proposed contribution and partner details
- Executed LLP agreement for the post-incorporation filing


Names, dates of birth and addresses should match across records. For foreign participation, confirm FEMA, FDI and beneficial-ownership requirements.


##


LLP Registration Cost and Timeline


There is no single fixed LLP registration cost. The total depends on factors such as the proposed contribution, MCA filing fees, name reservation, the number of DSCs, state stamp duty on the LLP agreement and professional fees.


The timeline also varies. Name objections, document mismatches, MCA resubmission requests and foreign-partner documentation can extend the process. Avoid promising a fixed two-to-four-week timeline without checking the case and current MCA processing conditions.


##


LLP Annual Compliance and Filing Requirements


An LLP must generally maintain proper books of account, file an income-tax return and complete its MCA filings even if it had limited or no business activity during the year.


### Form 11: Annual Return


Form 11 reports details of the LLP and its partners. For an LLP following the standard financial year ending 31 March, it is generally due within 60 days of the financial year-end, commonly 30 May, subject to MCA extensions or rule changes.


### Form 8: Statement of Account and Solvency


Form 8 contains financial information and a solvency declaration. For the standard financial year, it is generally due within 30 days after the end of six months from the financial year-end, commonly 30 October, subject to current rules and extensions.


### Audit and Other Obligations


Under current LLP rules, audit requirements are linked to prescribed turnover and contribution thresholds. The commonly applied thresholds are turnover above ₹40 lakh or contribution above ₹25 lakh, but the LLP should confirm the latest rules before relying on an exemption.


Other obligations may include[GST returns](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/gst-return-filing/) , TDS filings, income-tax audit requirements and event-based MCA forms for changes in partners, the agreement or registered office. Late-filing fees and penalties depend on the applicable law, filing period and type of default, so avoid using the outdated blanket claim of ₹100 per day with no cap.


##


Common LLP Registration and Compliance Mistakes


- Selecting a name that conflicts with an existing entity or trademark
- Filing identity documents with inconsistent names, addresses or dates of birth
- Omitting the owner’s NOC or a recent registered-office utility bill
- Treating a template LLP agreement as sufficient without defining authority and exit rights
- Missing the Form 3 deadline after incorporation
- Assuming an inactive LLP does not need annual filings
- Choosing an LLP despite a near-term need for equity shares, ESOPs or conventional venture capital


A practising company secretary, chartered accountant or lawyer can help assess the structure and prepare filings, but the partners should still understand the obligations they are accepting.


##


Who Should Choose an LLP?


An LLP can work well for consulting firms, agencies, professional practices, family-run businesses and bootstrapped ventures where a small group of partners intends to manage the business directly.


It may be less suitable when the business expects to issue equity shares, create an[ESOP pool](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/esop-full-form-meaning-how-esops-work-in-indian-startups/) or raise conventional venture capital. An LLP can still receive partner contributions, borrow and use other legally permitted financing, but it cannot issue company shares.


##


After LLP Registration: Prepare to Collect Payments


Once incorporated, an LLP usually needs a bank account, tax registrations and a payments setup suited to its sales channel. A website or app may need an online[payment gateway](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-gateway-india/) , while a consulting or invoice-led business may prefer[Payment Links](https://www.cashfree.com/payment-links/) . An LLP selling to overseas customers should separately assess its banking, FEMA and[international payment collection](https://www.cashfree.com/international-payment-gateway/) requirements.


Before applying, understand how the[merchant onboarding process](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/merchant-onboarding-process/) checks business, bank and website details.


##


Conclusion


An LLP combines legal identity, continuity and limited liability with agreement-led management. It suits closely held businesses whose partners want flexibility without automatic liability for one another’s conduct.


Before registering, compare the LLP with a partnership firm and private limited company, then review liability, taxation, funding plans and partner relationships.

##


Frequently Asked Questions


#### What is the full form of LLP?


LLP stands for Limited Liability Partnership. It is a separate legal entity that combines partner-led management with limited liability protection.


#### What is an LLP company?


“LLP company” is a common search term, but an LLP is not legally a company under the Companies Act. It is a body corporate registered under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008.


#### What is the liability of a partner in an LLP?


A partner is generally not personally liable for an LLP obligation solely because they are a partner. However, a partner remains liable for their own wrongful acts or omissions, and the liability shield can be lost in cases involving fraud or personal guarantees.


#### How is LLP liability different from partnership liability?


Partners in a traditional partnership may have unlimited personal liability for firm obligations. In an LLP, the entity normally bears its own liabilities, subject to statutory exceptions and each partner’s responsibility for their own conduct.


#### How many partners are required to form an LLP?


An LLP needs at least two partners and at least two designated partners. At least one designated partner must satisfy the current resident-in-India requirement under the LLP Act.


#### Is an LLP better than a private limited company?


Neither is universally better. An LLP may suit partner-managed businesses that value flexibility and limited liability. A private limited company is usually more suitable when issuing equity, offering ESOPs or raising institutional investment is central to the plan.


#### Can an LLP raise funding?


Yes, but not by issuing company shares. An LLP may receive partner contributions, borrow funds and use other permissible financing. Conventional venture capital investors often prefer a private limited company because it supports shares, preference instruments and clearer exit structures.


#### What annual forms does an LLP file?


The primary MCA annual filings are generally Form 11 and Form 8. Income-tax returns and applicable GST, TDS, audit or event-based filings may also be required.
